details.selection: Appointed Election Commissioner by the President on 31 Aug 2017 (Ministry of Law & Justice announcement) and took over as CEC on 2 Dec 2018 on the retirement of O.P. Rawat, as the senior Election Commissioner. No selection committee existed then. Before the 2023 Act there was no statute on selection: the Union government, by convention, picked senior serving or retired Secretary-rank officers and the President appointed on its advice, with the senior-most EC normally elevated to CEC (as described by the Supreme Court in Anoop Baranwal, 2 Mar 2023).
details.tenure_end: Demitted office on 12 Apr 2021 on completing his tenure at the age limit of 65.
details.education: B.A. (Hons) and M.A. in English, Panjab University (Hoshiarpur) - per ECI profile

entries.title: Arun Goel: Election Commissioner (2022-2024), resigned
entries.summary: Retired IAS officer of the Punjab cadre, 1985 batch, who took voluntary retirement as Secretary, Heavy Industries on 18 Nov 2022 and was appointed Election Commissioner the same day. Served from 21 Nov 2022 until he resigned with effect from 9 Mar 2024, days before the 2024 Lok Sabha schedule was announced. His term could have run to December 2027.

details.selection: On 18 Nov 2022 the Law Minister put up a panel of four names drawn from the IAS database, the Prime Minister recommended Goel, his voluntary retirement was accepted with the three-month notice waived, and his appointment was notified, all on the same day while a Constitution Bench was hearing petitions on how ECs should be appointed (Supreme Court, Anoop Baranwal, paras 187-195). The Court noted he was the youngest of the four and would get just over five years. Before the 2023 Act there was no statute on selection: the Union government, by convention, picked senior serving or retired Secretary-rank officers and the President appointed on its advice, with the senior-most EC normally elevated to CEC (as described by the Supreme Court in Anoop Baranwal, 2 Mar 2023).
details.tenure_end: Resigned; the President accepted the resignation with effect from 9 Mar 2024 under Section 11(1) of the 2023 Act (Gazette notification as quoted by The Tribune). No official reason was given. The Supreme Court judgment records he was due to retire from the IAS on 31 Dec 2022 at 60, so his EC term (to age 65) could have run to December 2027.
details.education: Post-graduate in Development Economics, Churchill College, Cambridge; M.Sc. Mathematics - per PIB

details.selection: EC (14 Mar 2024): chosen under the 2023 Act by a committee of PM Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah and Congress leader Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury from a six-name shortlist presented by Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal; Shah proposed Kumar and Sandhu; Chowdhury recorded dissent on procedure (Indian Express). CEC (17 Feb 2025): committee of Modi, Shah and LoP Rahul Gandhi; Gandhi submitted a dissent note and did not take part in further proceedings; the Law Ministry notification came late on 17 Feb (Tribune, DH).

entries.title: Lavasa writes to CEC seeking to record dissent on poll-code decisions
entries.summary: Election Commissioner Ashok Lavasa first wrote to CEC Sunil Arora on 4 May 2019 about Model Code of Conduct decisions, and later said he would stay away from meetings on code complaints until minority views were recorded in the Commission's orders. His dissents concerned complaints against PM Narendra Modi and BJP president Amit Shah, which the majority cleared.

entries.notes: The letters themselves are not public; accounts come from PTI and Deccan Herald. The Commission's legal division reportedly held that dissent on MCC decisions stays on file and is not made public.

entries.title: CEC Arora calls dissent row 'unsavoury', says members need not be clones
entries.summary: CEC Sunil Arora issued a statement calling the reported controversy over Lavasa's dissent unsavoury and avoidable, said Commission members are not expected to be clones of each other, and said the full Commission would meet on 21 May on the issue. Lavasa described the matter as internal.

entries.title: Arun Goel takes voluntary retirement and is appointed EC the same day
entries.summary: On 18 Nov 2022, the day after a Constitution Bench began hearing petitions on how Election Commissioners should be chosen, the government shortlisted four names, the PM recommended Arun Goel, his voluntary retirement as Heavy Industries Secretary was accepted with the notice period waived, and his appointment was notified. He took charge on 21 Nov 2022.

entries.title: Supreme Court records how Goel's appointment was compressed into one day
entries.summary: In Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India, the Constitution Bench set out the file history of Goel's appointment and said appointing officers who cannot serve the six-year term defeats the law's purpose and undermines the Commission's independence. It directed that, until Parliament legislated, the PM, the Leader of Opposition and the CJI would advise on appointments. It did not set aside Goel's appointment.

entries.title: Gyanesh Kumar and Sukhbir Sandhu appointed ECs under the 2023 Act

The appointments were notified in the Gazette that evening and both took charge on 15 Mar 2024.

entries.summary: The President appointed EC Gyanesh Kumar as the 26th CEC and Haryana Chief Secretary Vivek Joshi as Election Commissioner on the recommendation of the Modi-Shah-Gandhi committee; the Law Ministry notification came late on 17 Feb 2025. entries.title: Opposition MPs file first-ever notices to remove a sitting CEC
entries.summary: Opposition MPs submitted notices in both Houses seeking a motion to remove CEC Gyanesh Kumar, signed by 130 Lok Sabha and 63 Rajya Sabha members. The notice listed seven charges, including partisan conduct, obstruction of inquiries into alleged electoral fraud, and mass disenfranchisement through the SIR.

entries.title: Congress dossier revives 2006 Kerala PWD case; vigilance says closed
entries.summary: A Congress dossier on CEC Gyanesh Kumar claimed that a vigilance probe touching his time as Kerala PWD Secretary, after the 2006 death of a Malaysian contractor's manager, had stalled. Replying to a Newslaundry RTI request, Kerala's Vigilance Department said an enquiry had been held and closed after no irregularities were found.

entries.title: Report: ECs Sandhu and Joshi objected on record 14 times in 10 months
entries.summary: The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected in writing at least 14 times, between November 2025 and August 2026, to decisions and orders they said were issued without their knowledge. The objections covered a Form 6 change, the handling of additions and deletions, appeals filed in West Bengal, and centralised access to the roll database. It said both also wrote to the Cabinet Secretary about a change in work allocation.

entries.title: ECI says differing views are normal and its orders have full legal sanction
entries.summary: Responding to the report, the Commission said differing views are a normal part of deliberation in any institution, that all its orders follow statutory procedure and carry full legal sanction, and that all three commissioners and every officer may offer suggestions.
